title: Churches formed and baptism
summary: The disciples formed a church in the lands round about; repentant people were baptized and received the Holy Ghost.
characters: people who repented and were baptized

explicit_facts.text: The disciples formed a church of Christ in all the lands round about.
Those who came to them and truly repented were baptized in Jesus's name and received the Holy Ghost.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A baptismal gathering can show the disciples and people together near water; the text does not specify the baptism's location or method.
unspecified_visual_details: The disciples' identities, clothing, ages, and appearances; the number of people; the setting and method of baptism; any visible depiction of the Holy Ghost.

narration.text: the disciples of Jesus had formed a church of Christ

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Holy Ghost in a particular visible form; no form is described.

title: One people in justice and sharing
summary: Nephites and Lamanites were converted, dealt justly, and shared all things; there were no rich or poor, bond or free.

explicit_facts.text: In the thirty-sixth year, the people throughout the land, Nephites and Lamanites, were converted to the Lord, and there were no contentions or disputations; each dealt justly with the others.
They had all things in common; there were no rich or poor, bond or free, and all were made free and partakers of the heavenly gift.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A peaceful gathering in which people share goods can convey the stated common ownership.
unspecified_visual_details: Which individuals are present, the specific goods shared, clothing, architecture, and any visible form for the heavenly gift.

narration.text: they had all things common among them

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict conversion or the heavenly gift as an unmentioned supernatural visual event.

title: Peace and the disciples' works
summary: Peace continued in the land. The disciples healed the sick, raised the dead, helped the lame walk, and enabled the blind and deaf to perceive.

explicit_facts.text: Peace continued in the land as the thirty-seventh year passed.
The disciples performed miracles, including healing the sick, raising the dead, causing the lame to walk, and enabling the blind to see and the deaf to hear; they worked miracles in Jesus's name.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A single healing can be shown as one representative instance of the listed works.
unspecified_visual_details: Which miracle to depict, the identities and number of those involved, and any visible form for divine power.

narration.text: they did heal the sick

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports multiple miracles across the period; a single image should represent one event, not imply all occurred simultaneously.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a visible divine figure or supernatural effect not described.

title: Cities rebuilt
summary: After many years, people prospered and rebuilt cities where cities had been burned, including Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: Many years passed, through the fifty-ninth year and beyond.
The Lord prospered the people, and they rebuilt cities where cities had been burned.
They rebuilt the great city Zarahemla.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Construction activity in Zarahemla can represent the rebuilding described.
unspecified_visual_details: The city's design, the nature of the construction, and the builders' identities and appearances.

narration.text: they did build cities again

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage does not describe the earlier burning as happening in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a city being burned or destroyed in the present scene.

title: Cities beneath the waters
summary: Some cities had sunk, and waters occupied their former places; those cities could not be renewed.

explicit_facts.text: Many cities had sunk, waters came up in their stead, and those cities could not be renewed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Water covering the former site of a city can illustrate the reported condition.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities' names, location, appearance, depth, and whether any structures remain visible.

narration.text: waters came up in the stead thereof

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a report of a past condition, not a newly occurring sinking.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a city sinking in the present scene.

title: Growing and forming families
summary: The people of Nephi grew strong, multiplied exceedingly fast, became fair and delightsome, were married and given in marriage, and were blessed according to the Lord's promises.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Nephi grew strong, multiplied exceedingly fast, and became fair and delightsome.
They were married and given in marriage, and were blessed according to the multitude of the Lord's promises to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group of people may represent the people of Nephi without implying that all marriages occurred at one time.
unspecified_visual_details: Individual identities, clothing, appearance, marriage customs, and setting.

narration.text: And they were married, and given in marriage,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blessings are reported, not described as a visible divine appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific couples, ceremonies, a single simultaneous marriage gathering, or a visible appearance of the Lord.

title: Meeting in prayer
summary: The people followed the commandments, fasting, praying, and meeting often to pray and hear the word of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: They no longer followed the performances and ordinances of the law of Moses; they followed the commandments, continued in fasting and prayer, and often met to pray and hear the Lord's word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathered community in prayer can depict one of the meetings described.
unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place, number and identities of attendees, speaker, and any specific ritual.

narration.text: continuing in fasting and prayer

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a continuing practice, not a particular dated meeting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a named speaker or specific ceremony not supplied.

title: A century of peace and succession
summary: Peace and love prevailed for generations. At a hundred years, the chosen disciples had gone to God's paradise except the three who should tarry; other disciples were ordained in their stead.

explicit_facts.text: There was no contention among the people, and mighty miracles were wrought among Jesus's disciples.
By a hundred years, Jesus's chosen disciples had gone to God's paradise except the three who should tarry; other disciples were ordained in their stead, and many of that generation had passed away.
There was no contention because God's love dwelt in the people's hearts.
There were no envyings, strifes, tumults, whoredoms, lyings, murders, or lasciviousness; the people were exceedingly happy.
There were no robbers or murderers, nor any manner of “—ites”; the people were one, children of Christ and heirs to God's kingdom.
The people were blessed and prospered until a hundred and ten years had passed, and there was no contention in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ordination of other disciples can be shown as a gathering of people around them.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner or place of ordination, identities of the other disciples, and how the chosen disciples went to paradise.

narration.text: there were no envyings, nor strifes

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The centuries of peace and the succession are reported over time; do not combine them into one literal moment.
“Gone to the paradise of God” does not specify a visible transition.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the chosen disciples ascending, dying, or appearing in paradise; no such event or appearance is described.

title: Nephi's record passes to Amos
summary: Nephi, keeper of the record, died; his son Amos kept the record on the plates of Nephi in his stead.
characters: Nephi, keeper of the last record

explicit_facts.text: Nephi, who kept the last record on the plates of Nephi, died; his son Amos kept it in his stead on those plates.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amos holding or attending to the plates can suggest his keeping the record.
unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances and place of Nephi's death, the appearance of either man, and the plates' design.

narration.text: his son Amos kept it in his stead

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The death and the record-keeping succession are stated; their precise timing within the verse is not elaborated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a deathbed, funeral, or conversation.

title: Lamanites appear again
summary: After Amos kept the record for eighty-four years, a small part of the people revolted from the church and took the name Lamanites; peace otherwise continued.
characters: people who revolted from the church

explicit_facts.text: Amos kept the record for eighty-four years, and peace continued except for a small part of the people who revolted from the church and took the name Lamanites.
The passage says there began to be Lamanites again in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A small group separating from a larger community may convey the reported revolt.
unspecified_visual_details: Amos's presence during the revolt, the group's appearance, and where the separation occurred.

narration.text: there began to be Lamanites again

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The revolt is reported, not described as a particular confrontation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or assign motives beyond the stated revolt.

title: Amos succeeds Amos
summary: Amos died in the year 194 from Christ's coming, and his son Amos kept the record in his stead. By the year 200, the second generation had passed away save a few.

explicit_facts.text: In the year 194 from Christ's coming, Amos died, and his son Amos kept the record in his stead on the plates of Nephi.
By the year 200, the second generation had passed away save a few.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The record being kept by the younger Amos can be shown with the plates.
unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances of Amos's death, the younger Amos's appearance, and who the few survivors were.

narration.text: his son Amos kept the record in his stead

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage gives distinct time markers; do not depict the second generation's passing as part of the record transfer.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a death scene or identify the few who remained.

title: People spread across the land
summary: Mormon reports that the people had multiplied and spread across the land, becoming exceedingly rich through their prosperity in Christ.

explicit_facts.text: The people had multiplied, spread over all the land, and become exceedingly rich because of their prosperity in Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A broad view of settlements and people across a landscape can suggest their spread.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific settlements, people, goods, clothing, and the appearance of the landscape.

narration.text: they were spread upon all the face of the land

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is Mormon's retrospective report, not a single expansion event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray prosperity in Christ as a visible supernatural effect.

title: Pride and costly things
summary: In the year 201, some became proud, wearing costly apparel and fine pearls; their goods were no longer held in common.

explicit_facts.text: In the year 201, some were lifted up in pride, wearing costly apparel, fine pearls, and worldly fine things.
From then on, they no longer had their goods and substance in common.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A person wearing fine apparel and pearls can represent the stated new display of wealth.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific garments, jewelry designs, individuals, and how private ownership was arranged.

narration.text: the wearing of costly apparel

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign named identities or motives beyond the stated pride.

title: Classes and self-built churches
summary: People divided into classes and built churches for gain, denying Christ's true church. By year 210, many churches professed Christ while denying much of his gospel.

explicit_facts.text: People divided into classes, built churches unto themselves to get gain, and began to deny the true church of Christ.
By the year 210, many churches professed to know Christ but denied much of his gospel, received wickedness, and administered sacred things to the unworthy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathering divided into visibly distinct groups can illustrate the reported classes.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and design of churches, the exact classes, and the administration of sacred things.

narration.text: they began to be divided into classes

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report developments over time; do not make the practices of year 210 occur in the same moment as the earlier division.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific sacred rite or identify those deemed unworthy.

title: Persecution and prison deliverance
summary: A church grew through iniquity and Satan's influence. Another church denied Christ and persecuted the true church; disciples who tarried were imprisoned, then the prison was rent in twain and they went forth doing miracles.
characters: members of the church that grew through iniquity
members of the church that denied Christ

explicit_facts.text: A church multiplied exceedingly because of iniquity and Satan's power over their hearts.
Another church denied Christ, persecuted the true church because of its humility and belief in Christ, and despised its miracles.
They exercised authority over the disciples who tarried and cast them into prison; the prison was rent in twain by the power of God's word within them, and they went forth doing mighty miracles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prison scene may show the disciples going forth through a divided prison structure.
unspecified_visual_details: The disciples' identities, prison design, manner of imprisonment, and any visible representation of God's word or Satan's power.

narration.text: they did cast them into prison

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize persecution and growth before describing the imprisonment and release; do not conflate those developments into one simultaneous act.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Satan as a visible figure; no appearance is described.

title: The people seek the disciples' lives
summary: Despite the miracles, the people hardened their hearts and sought to kill the disciples, as Jesus had said.
characters: people seeking to kill the disciples

explicit_facts.text: Despite the miracles, the people hardened their hearts and sought to kill the disciples, as the Jews at Jerusalem had sought to kill Jesus according to his word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A hostile group confronting disciples can represent the attempt described.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, weapons, identities, and whether a specific attack occurred.

narration.text: did seek to kill them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports intent; it does not narrate a completed killing or specify a particular confrontation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a killing, injury, or a separate scene in Jerusalem.

title: Cast into fire
summary: The disciples were cast into furnaces of fire and came forth unharmed.
characters: people who cast them into furnaces

explicit_facts.text: The people cast the disciples into furnaces of fire, and the disciples came forth receiving no harm.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The disciples can be shown emerging from a furnace, with no visible injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The furnace construction, number of disciples and people, and how they emerged unharmed.

narration.text: they came forth receiving no harm

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict injuries, burns, or an unmentioned visible miracle effect.

title: Among wild beasts
summary: The disciples were cast into dens of wild beasts, played with the beasts as a child with a lamb, and came forth unharmed.
characters: people who cast them into dens

explicit_facts.text: The people cast the disciples into dens of wild beasts; the disciples played with the beasts as a child with a lamb and came forth unharmed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The disciples can be shown calmly among wild beasts, without depicting an attack.
unspecified_visual_details: The species and number of beasts, the den's appearance, and the disciples' identities.

narration.text: they did play with the wild beasts

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack, injury, or gore.

title: Violence against the people of Jesus
summary: False priests and prophets led people into iniquity and many churches. The people smote the people of Jesus, who did not strike back; unbelief and wickedness increased through year 230.
characters: people who smote the people of Jesus

explicit_facts.text: Many priests and false prophets led the people to build churches and commit iniquity.
The people smote the people of Jesus, who did not smite again.
They dwindled in unbelief and wickedness from year to year until 230 years had passed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A single instance of an attacker striking and the other person not retaliating can illustrate the stated action.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities, number, location, and nature of the blows.

narration.text: the people of Jesus did not smite again

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a pattern over years; show one instance only, not the full period as a single event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show injury, blood, or retaliation.

title: A great division
summary: In year 231 a great division arose. True believers in Christ were called Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites; the three disciples who should tarry were among the true worshipers.
characters: the three disciples who should tarry

explicit_facts.text: In year 231, a great division arose among the people.
A people called Nephites arose as true believers in Christ; among them were those called Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites by the Lamanites.
True believers and worshipers of Christ, including the three disciples who should tarry, were called Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group gathered apart from another can suggest the division, without implying a specific confrontation.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and number of each group and the precise nature of the division.

narration.text: there was a great division among the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The labels for the groups are reported names, not evidence of separate events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named individual members or portray the three disciples' identities beyond the supplied description.

title: Those who reject the gospel
summary: Those rejecting the gospel were called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites; they rebelled, taught their children not to believe, and taught hatred of God's children.

explicit_facts.text: Those who rejected the gospel were called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites; they wilfully rebelled and taught their children not to believe.
Because of their fathers' wickedness, they were taught to hate God's children, as the Lamanites had been taught to hate Nephi's children from the beginning.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An adult teaching children can represent the reported instruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The individuals, the setting, and the words used in the teaching.

narration.text: they did teach their children that they should not believe

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earlier teaching is summarized; do not stage the distant historical comparison as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or depict the earlier Lamanite-Nephi conflict.

title: The more wicked become numerous
summary: By year 244, the more wicked people had become much more numerous than God's people. They continued building and adorning churches as years 250 and 260 passed.
characters: the more wicked part of the people

explicit_facts.text: By year 244, the more wicked part had grown strong and become much more numerous than God's people.
They continued building churches and adorning them with precious things; years 250 and 260 passed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A church adorned with precious things can illustrate the building and adornment reported.
unspecified_visual_details: The church design, precious objects, and the groups' exact numbers and appearances.

narration.text: became exceedingly more numerous than were the people of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses span years 244 through 260; do not show the increase and later adornment as one instantaneous event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not attribute individual identities or a specific church denomination.

people called the people of Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent an oath, ritual, emblem, or named member.

title: The disciples sorrow

reasonable_visual_inferences: The disciples may be shown in a solemn gathering to convey sorrow.
unspecified_visual_details: The disciples' identities, what occasioned their sorrow in a particular moment, and their expressions or setting.

narration.text: the disciples began to sorrow for the sins of the world

title: Robbers spread across the land
summary: Gadianton robbers spread across the land; only the disciples were righteous. People stored abundant gold and silver and engaged in trade.

explicit_facts.text: Gadianton robbers spread across all the land, and none were righteous except the disciples of Jesus.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A trading scene with stored precious metals can represent the reported commerce.
unspecified_visual_details: The traders' identities, specific goods, locations, and the robbers' appearance or actions.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific robbery or identify unnamed people as Gadianton members.

title: Ammaron keeps the record

unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances and place of Amos's death, the record's appearance, and the brothers' appearances.

title: Ammaron hides the sacred records
summary: In year 320, constrained by the Holy Ghost, Ammaron hid the sacred records for the Lord, that they might return to Jacob's remnant according to the Lord's prophecies and promises.

explicit_facts.text: In year 320, constrained by the Holy Ghost, Ammaron hid the sacred records handed down through generations.

unspecified_visual_details: The hiding place, method, appearance and number of records, and any visible form of the Holy Ghost.
